## How it works

<h3>Try it</h3><ol><li>Use the map to locate the bridge relative to the roads and river.</li><li>Open View at the top right → Layers and choose Satellite or Street to compare the model with the surrounding area.</li><li>Zoom between the bridge and its wider setting.</li></ol><h2>Developer integration</h2><p>After <code>viewer.add()</code>, call <code>viewer.toggleMap(true)</code> to show the project's map context. The SDK owns map styles and terrain controls. The source placement and height limitations are listed under Model notes.</p><p>Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example <code>python -m http.server 8080</code>. Open <code>http://localhost:8080/</code>; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.</p>
<p>The host uses <code>await viewer.IfcAPI</code> to open the hash-verified source, writes the projected CRS vertical datum with <code>WriteLine()</code>, and saves the edited bytes with <code>SaveModel()</code>. It closes the native model and disposes WASM before <code>viewer.add()</code>. See the <a href="https://thatopen.github.io/engine_web-ifc/docs/classes/web-ifc.IfcAPI.html">complete web-ifc API reference</a>.</p><h3>Model notes</h3><p>Height datum set to NAP (inferred); geometry retained. The publisher reports a small XYZ offset. Optional terrain is a 30 m surface.</p>

<h2>Sources and license notices</h2><p><a href="https://github.com/Geonovum/GeoBIM_Georefereren/blob/0fe0f5e89676de3d21fc3219eb5805b36e29e032/data/voorbeeldmodellen_Infra/Van%20Brienenoordbrug-IFC4X3.ifc" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Geonovum and original model authors</a> · <a href="https://github.com/Geonovum/GeoBIM_Georefereren/blob/0fe0f5e89676de3d21fc3219eb5805b36e29e032/LICENSE" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W3C</a></p>
<p>The example supplements the missing vertical datum as NAP, inferred from the publisher’s successful height validation against AHN (NAP). Original geometry, map-conversion coordinates and heights are retained. The publisher reports a small XYZ offset against AHN. Copernicus is a 30 m surface model, so this is not a certified survey overlay.</p>
